capability_groups.label: Pre-processing: audit and repair the data

ci.note: Measured by CI with pytest --cov across the full dependency matrix on three interpreters. It is not recomputed on every docs build, so it is published AS OF the date above rather than as a live figure. The fix for a stale number is a date, not a silent refresh.

test_composition.note: Split by name, a heuristic, so the vocabulary is published with the figure. It says which tests are ABOUT honest refusal, not which are good.

states.DEFECT OPEN: proved by execution to report a value nobody measured
states.NOT A MEASUREMENT: produces no fairness number and no verdict, so the defect class cannot apply; assigned only after running it
states.PROVEN: refuses honestly when nothing is measurable, measures correctly when something is, and a test holds it there
states.SEMI-PROVEN: behaves honestly today, verified by execution, but no pin fails when it regresses

criteria.name: Every public code unit carries a grade
criteria.why: An ungraded code unit is not a clean one. It is the absence of a measurement, and it is where every defect this campaign found was living: in code nobody had ever run on undefined input.

criteria.name: Every grade was confirmed by an independent check
criteria.why: 291 of 872 grades were overturned when an independent agent was told to refute them. A grade nobody checked is a claim, not a measurement, and at that rate a large share of them are wrong.

criteria.name: No open defect anywhere in the public surface
criteria.why: The product promise is that this library does not report a number nobody measured. An open defect of that class contradicts the promise wherever it sits, not only inside the capability census.

criteria.name: Every open defect has an assessed severity
criteria.why: Severity decides ORDER, never whether. An unassessed severity is recorded as blocking: not having looked at a defect is not evidence that it is minor.

criteria.name: Capability census complete and clear
criteria.why: The 215 capabilities are the surface a user reaches on purpose. This is the criterion that already passes, and on its own it was never sufficient to call the library ready.

beta_criteria.name: Every public code unit has been EXECUTED and its result recorded
beta_criteria.why: An unexamined code unit is the absence of a measurement, and it is where every defect this campaign found was living. Counted here: the capability census, the grading waves, the surface probe AND the test suite, which executes most of the surface and was credited for none of it until 2026-09-25. What remains is the genuinely untouched pile. See B1b for the disclosure half.
beta_criteria.plain: Has every public unit actually been RUN, with the result written down? Not a belief that it works: executed, by the suite or an audit, and recorded.

beta_criteria.name: Every public code unit's examination state is PUBLISHED where it is described
beta_criteria.why: The clause the beta tier's own definition ends with, and the one that decides whether an unexamined unit can mislead anybody: not that everything was checked, but that nothing unchecked is presented as checked. Each row states which of the three states it is in and, when it is unexamined, why. Enforced by scripts/capability_status.py --check, scripts/stamp_status_badges.py --check and tests/test_capability_status_badges.py, each sabotage-tested.
beta_criteria.plain: Can a reader SEE that state where the unit is described? A measurement nobody can find is the defect this library is audited for.

beta_criteria.name: No open defect in code that returns a fairness number or verdict
beta_criteria.why: This is the defect that reaches a user as a false clean bill. A code unit whose return type nobody has classified counts here too: not having worked out what it returns is not evidence that it is harmless.
beta_criteria.plain: Is anything still broken in code that hands back a fairness number or a verdict? This is the defect that reaches a user as a false clean bill.

beta_criteria.name: No open defect recorded by the second-round audit
beta_criteria.why: ADDED 2026-09-28, because B2 read 0 open while 35 execution-proven defects were open. B2 counts DEFECT OPEN rows in the grading waves, and the second-round audit's findings are not in those waves: they are in tests/test_bgl6_*.py, one test per claim, each asserting the value the unit produces today. So the gate could say 'no open defect in code that returns a fairness number' while a probe cleared a scaffolded model and a benchmark certified a model that decided nothing. A gate that cannot see a whole body of findings reports a pass it has not earned, which is the defect class this library is audited for, in the gate itself.
beta_criteria.plain: The fix wave was audited a SECOND time, by agents attacking the fixes. Every open record is a test that reproduces its defect today.

beta_criteria.name: Every remaining open defect carries an assessed severity
beta_criteria.why: A beta may ship with known defects. It may not ship with defects nobody has looked at hard enough to rank, because severity decides order and an unranked defect never gets an order.
beta_criteria.plain: Every defect still open has to carry a severity. A beta may ship with known defects; it may not ship with ones nobody has ranked.

beta_criteria.name: Capability census complete and clear
beta_criteria.why: The 215 capabilities are the surface a user reaches on purpose and they carry the product promise directly.
beta_criteria.plain: The registered capabilities are the surface a user reaches on purpose, so the census over them has to be complete and clear.

beta_criteria.name: Same answer as an established library, where one exists
beta_criteria.measured: 34 of 34 agree; 76 have no outside reference
beta_criteria.why: Agreement with fairlearn, scikit-learn, statsmodels or scipy on clean data is the only correctness evidence that does not come from this project itself.
beta_criteria.plain: Where an established library computes the same number, does vfairness give the same answer on clean data?

beta_criteria.name: No invented number on broken data
beta_criteria.measured: 109 of 109 measuring capabilities pass; 0 fabricate, 0 over-refuse, 0 not covered
beta_criteria.why: A number where nothing was measurable reads as a clean bill. This is the defect the whole hardening programme was about.
beta_criteria.plain: Does every capability that measures refuse to invent a number when the data cannot support one, and still measure when it can?
